name: Work set by a reader, made in Wizzad and defended

issuer.name: Wizzad
issuer.description: Wizzad issues this credential from the student’s study record: counts, dates and methods, fixed when the task was finished and defended. It is not a grade, a verdict or an identity check.

evidence.name: The student’s study record: the task, the making and the defense
evidence.description: The student’s study record shows the reader’s task as set, how the page was made in Wizzad, and the defense, each digitally signed. The student shares the record on a link of their own; this credential carries no link.

evidence.name: The signed defense record
evidence.description: The defense was sealed as one object and signed with the same key that signs this credential; the record the student shares serves that object, its signature and the id of the key.

credentialSubject.narrative: Written in Wizzad over 1 sitting on 1 day — 2 saves on 20 September 2026. Of everything added, 100% was typed. The version defended is one of the saved states. Without the piece in front of them: 4 of 4 factual questions answered correctly; 2 of 2 explanations graded as full; 1 of 1 changes to the piece accounted for; a second AI grader agreed on 3 of 3. Finished 20 September 2026 · begun to finished: 10 min · defended 1 min after finishing · identified by signed-in account · answered in writing · digitally signed

achievement.name: Task set by a reader: In about 300 words, explain what you mean by bridges and…

criteria.narrative: Made in Wizzad’s own editor with the reader’s task pinned above it, in one sitting of up to 90 minutes, begun within a week of being set. Wizzad recorded the making as it does for any page: the sittings, and the characters typed, pasted or written with its assistant. On finishing, the version was sealed and defended at once in a timed session with the piece out of sight — questions drawn from the piece and from how it was made, checked automatically or graded by an AI grader against a marking guide. The task, the making and the defense were signed together as one record.

achievement.description: The task, as set: “In about 300 words, explain what you mean by bridges and boats having the same honesty, with one concrete example from engineering that you have not used in your essay.”
